experiment: P3o-D frozen frequency recognition with posterior-conditioned delay parameter residual
research_question: With a local time-frequency recognition backbone, can a delay-peak residual parameter side branch improve twelve-parameter sensing without changing any recognition logit, safe threshold, low-power recognition metric, or worst-combination parameter risk?
hypothesis: A posterior-conditioned delay residual can add parameter information only where the frozen frequency backbone has class evidence, avoiding the early-fusion trade-off that degraded 25 dB recognition in P3o-C.

identity_protocol.identity_pairing: receiver_noise_seed grouped across regimes and power views

methods.F_frozen_base: P3o-C local STFT plus adjacent-frame phase-increment backbone, trained with BCEWithLogits + 0.1 masked SmoothL1.
methods.F_delay_parameter_residual: The selected F_frozen_base is entirely frozen. Its logits, classifier and base parameter prediction are copied exactly. A delay-peak encoder predicts a classwise residual, multiplied by detached sigmoid(logit) and added only to the parameter prediction.

base.checkpoint: C_joint: maximum early macro-AUPR among epochs with oracle parameter NMAE <= 1.01 times minimum

residual.checkpoint: minimum early oracle parameter NMAE; classification path is fixed

training.calibration: Reuse each selected frozen-base threshold vector verbatim. The residual method must not recalibrate or select from development.

decision_rule: Only if every gate passes may 1090M/1100M be generated for confirmation. Otherwise freeze failure, do not use confirmation identities, and do not tune 1080M.
